answer: Stake-weighted identity is one way an agent economy can blunt sybil attacks. Each agent locks a bond tied to a verified operator key before it can attest or grade, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs real capital. Bonds are slashed when peers prove misconduct. Like pigment in a dye, the bond gives every identity a costly mark that is hard to copy, and like onyx it stays hard to fake under pressure. Reaching the summit of trust then takes sustained honest work, not a burst of accounts.
